styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Vasa Museum, Gamla Stan lanes and modern art in one loop.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Royal Palace, old town and the archipelago's story.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Ferries, green islands and water everywhere.

stays.why: Central and practical. Walk to Gamla Stan and the station; most metro lines meet here.
Sleep in the old town. Pretty lanes, but noisy in summer and few lifts in old buildings.
Cafés, bars and viewpoints. A short metro or walk south of the centre; good value.
Quiet, upmarket and close to Djurgården's museums and parkland.

food: Try Swedish classics: meatballs with lingonberry, pickled herring, and cinnamon buns (kanelbullar).
Lunch is the value meal. Many restaurants serve a weekday 'dagens lunch' for around SEK 120–160.
Fika is a coffee-and-pastry break. Sit down mid-afternoon like the locals do.
Södermalm and Vasastan have the best casual food streets; book dinner spots ahead on weekends.
Alcohol is expensive and sold in state shops (Systembolaget). Check opening hours before you shop.
more_time: Take a ferry to Djurgården for the Vasa Museum and Skansen if you have a spare half-day.
Swap a city afternoon for a short archipelago boat trip; check timetables and weather on the day.
Rainy day? The metro art walk and the City Hall tour fill a few hours cheaply.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Vasa Museum, Gamla Stan and a ferry; add a night for the archipelago or a slower museum day.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near 1°C and lows around -4°C. Pack warm layers and expect short daylight.
February: still cold, highs near 2°C. Fewer crowds; museums are calm.
March: slowly warming, highs near 5°C, but nights still below freezing. Watch for icy pavements.
April: highs near 10°C. Pleasant for walking; keep a rain jacket handy.
May: mild and bright, highs near 16°C. Great for ferries and parks.
June: warm, highs near 21°C. Long days; pack for occasional showers.
July: warmest month, highs near 22°C, but the most rain days. Book hotels early.
August: warm at about 21°C. Still busy; evenings cool down.
September: highs near 17°C. Comfortable and quieter; good for walking.
October: cooler, highs near 11°C. Bring a warm layer and an umbrella.
November: cold and grey, highs near 5°C. Short days; plan indoor sights.
December: cold, highs near 2°C. Dark early; dress for wind and damp.

climate_guide.summary: Northern coastal climate: cold winters, mild summers, and rain spread across the year.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Highs from about 16°C to 22°C. Long daylight makes walking and ferries easy.

items.title: Winter is cold (Dec–Feb)
items.text: Highs near 1–2°C and lows around -4°C. Pack a warm coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: About 8–12 rain days each month. July is the wettest. Carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Mild summer, not hot
items.text: July highs near 22°C. Evenings can be cool, so bring a light layer.

items.title: Big daylight swing
items.text: Very long days in June, very short in December. Plan winter sightseeing for midday.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes. Add warm winter gear from November to March.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; walk in the centre and take ferries for the islands.

modes.text: The Tunnelbana is fast and covers the city. Buy an SL card or use the app.
Trams and buses fill the gaps. The SL travel card is best value.
Taxis are pricey. Use Uber or Bolt for app-based rides.
Driving is not recommended in the centre due to congestion and tolls.
Walking and cycling are great in warm months, with many bike lanes.
Ferries connect the islands and are part of the transit network.
